cards.factual_support: The ET summary explicitly supports September 6.7 percent growth, four-month low, high-base and mining explanation, manufacturing 7.6 percent year-on-year, and increased electricity generation. Attribution retained; the GDP forecast above 7 percent is not presented as an actual result.
cards.analysis: Sector divergence is an interpretation of the captured components, not an extra statistic. The next-signal sentence asks about the next mining and manufacturing readings and asserts no future recovery.
cards.novelty: All 76 history records checked: the previously published September core-industries 7.9 percent index is a different statistical release, while this is the broader IIP event. Four alternate IIP records link to this representative, leaving only one card.

cards.factual_support: The title supplies Cabinet approval and Rs10000 crore. The summary supplies support through 2039-40 and the tenfold 750000 TEU target. The brief calls capacity an aim and never describes factories or financing disbursement as completed.
cards.analysis: Cost competitiveness is conditional on bridging the cited cost gap. Watching support terms and subsequent usable capacity distinguishes the approved scheme from actual output without adding dates or eligibility rules.
cards.novelty: No container-manufacturing approval exists in history; the earlier SME Growth Fund also cost Rs10000 crore but has a different object. Three other captured scheme reports are explicitly clustered behind this representative.

cards.factual_support: Fiscal horizon 2033-34 comes from the preserved title; the summary's until-2034 wording is compatible. The Rs200-to-Rs100 crore turnover change applies only to certain manufacturers, and November 1 to December 31 is the future application window, not completed submissions.
cards.analysis: Potential broader eligibility follows from the lower threshold without claiming all MSMEs qualify. The watch asks for actual applicant participation and commitments, making the incentive-to-investment channel observable.
cards.novelty: The ledger contains no textiles PLI extension or threshold change. The existing electronics PLI commentary in the pool concerns another industry and supplies no same-event duplication.

cards.factual_support: ET supports Cabinet approval of a 3 percent DA increase, retrospective July 1 effect, expected over-11.6-million beneficiaries and Rs10016 crore cost. The brief neither calls the hike three percentage points nor states that arrears have been paid.
cards.analysis: Household cash flow and fiscal spending are conditional consequences of the approved allowance. Watching payment timing explicitly recognises the gap between authorisation and receipt.
cards.novelty: No DA increase exists in the ledger. The social-assistance programme and senior-citizen fund release have different beneficiaries and instruments; two direct DA reports are grouped rather than occupying extra cards.

cards.factual_support: The original summary names the Indian Patent Office, Tuesday rejection, BPaL, three medicines, six-month drug-resistant TB treatment and the opposing groups' joint statement. The brief preserves that source chain; no drug names, efficacy rates, prices or finality beyond this application are invented.
cards.analysis: The supply mechanism is explicitly possible, not a guarantee that all patents have disappeared or medicines become cheaper. Future challenges and supplier announcements are signals, not reported events.
cards.novelty: No BPaL or TB patent decision appears in the ledger. Earlier FSSAI nutrition notices concern a different regulator and action; cancer medicine price cuts in this pool are separate eligible alternatives.

cards.factual_support: The title identifies Supreme Court and UAPA; the summary confines the statutory bar to unauthorised or illegal entry. The two brief sentences retain this condition and do not promise bail for all lawfully entered foreigners or remove other statutory tests.
cards.analysis: The mechanism addresses this particular bar, while the next signal explicitly retains other applicable requirements. Neither sentence expands the ruling into automatic release or a general exemption from UAPA.
cards.novelty: Checked against previous false-affidavit, custodial-interrogation, trafficking and other court decisions in history: none concerns the foreign-national entry condition for this bail bar. The evidence remains within the live 36-hour window.

cards.factual_support: The title supports PhonePe's rebrand and expansion; the summary supports more than 200 million devices through OEM partnerships, gift cards, top-ups and a webstore. Device presence is not called active users, transactions, paying customers or completed monetisation.
cards.analysis: Additional transaction channels are a conditional commercial inference from the named goods and webstore. Watching repeat purchases and developer participation tests whether distribution converts to usage without inventing conversion data.
cards.novelty: No Indus Appstore rebrand or digital-goods expansion exists in history. Google's Registered App Stores rollout is a separate eligible platform event; foreign app-store penalties are another jurisdiction and not duplicates of PhonePe's action.
